page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is an entry-level general purpose compute instance built on the ARMv8 architecture. Powered by an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, the instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, mapping directly to 2 vCPUs. The hardware includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server configuration includes no integrated local storage, lacks dedicated GPUs, and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements position the t2a-standard-2 primarily in the lower tiers across compute-intensive tasks, largely due to its modest two-core footprint. The server logged a Geekbench single-core score of 1,101.0 and a multi-core score of 1,997.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 1,596.29. Computational compression throughput varies, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 1,812.29 and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 24.01 GB/sec, reflecting average single-thread behavior. However, multi-threaded decompression drops to 16.52 GB/sec in bzip3 tests, placing it in the bottom 10% of evaluated systems.

Memory subsystem testing reveals uncached large-block read bandwidth of 26.99 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 16.42 GB/sec, resulting in a PassMark memory score of 858.29. Application benchmarks recorded static web serving throughput at 2.66 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 2.61 million operations per second. Hardware-level encryption instructions (AES) are supported, but modern x86 vector instruction sets like AVX, AVX-512, and AMX are absent given the ARM platform.

Given its dedicated core allocation and modest resource footprint, the t2a-standard-2 provides a predictable execution environment for lightweight cloud workloads. It is best suited for small-scale web serving, light application testing, continuous integration tasks, and basic development environments that benefit from ARM64 architecture without requiring high memory throughput or massive parallel compute capacity.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is a general-purpose instance featuring 2 dedicated ARM64 vCPUs powered by a 3.0 GHz Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor. It includes 8.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per core), 32 MB of L3 cache, and lacks local disk storage or GPU acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the instance delivers average single-thread compute capabilities, achieving a stress-ng single-core rating of 1,812.29 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,101.0, though overall multi-core and memory subsystem throughput fall into lower percentiles with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1,997.0 and large-block read speeds of 26.99 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput measures 2.61 million operations per second alongside 2.66 GB/sec static web serving bandwidth. The t2a-standard-2 is best deployed for lightweight web serving, ARM-targeted software development, CI pipelines, and small internal utility services.
